design_fidelity.notes: Implementation matches the design doc line for line: GOLDEN_SETUP and its order, SETUP_S=600 / DL_S=3600 defaults, the 9-line bounded helper, every make call moved onto bounded (runtime, sky-assets, test, each setup target, golden), the exact failure strings and the golden-only path (no setup) vs golden path (setup then golden). The two extra hang cases (test-hang, golden-hang, the latter with a TERM-ignoring child) and the reaper positive control go beyond the doc in the right direction.

findings.summary: A non-positive bound silently disables the timer: bounded() calls 'alarm $s', and alarm 0 (or a negative value) cancels the alarm, so RIG_SETUP_S=0 / RIG_DL_S=0 / RIG_TEST_S=0 / RIG_GOLDEN_S=0 turns a bounded make into an unbounded one with no message.
findings.evidence: Judge probe P9 (scratch /tmp/claude/rg-eval/probe2.sh, bounded() extracted verbatim from tools/rig_check.sh): 'bounded 0 sh -c "sleep 3"' returned rc 0 after the full sleep instead of 124; the same helper returned 124 for 'bounded 1 ...' (probe P3). Defaults (600/3600/7200/1800) are unaffected.

findings.summary: bounded() only cleans the process group on timeout or interrupt; a command that exits 0 while leaving a background grandchild leaks it, outside the rig's cleanup and outside the clone.
findings.evidence: Judge probe P8: 'bounded 5 sh -c "sleep 30 & exit 0"' returned rc 0 and the orphan 'sleep 30' (pid 91433) was still alive afterwards. No current make recipe backgrounds a process, so the impact today is nil.

findings.summary: If the rig shell itself is terminated while bounded is inside its TERM->KILL 2 s window, the EXIT trap ('cd / && rm -rf "$dir"') deletes the clone before the process group is KILLed, so the still-running make can fail noisily against a deleted directory. The group is still KILLed 2 s later, so nothing leaks; the ordering is cosmetic.
findings.evidence: Code read: the trap is installed before the clone (tools/rig_check.sh:70) and the handler's cleanup is 'kill TERM; sleep 2; kill KILL' (tools/rig_check.sh:35-36); judge probes P7b/P7c confirm that TERM/INT delivered to the perl wrapper itself does exit 130 and kills the group child.

findings.summary: Coverage note: the hermetic control rides 'make test' (mk/m45.mk:57) but is not part of the ci-fast tier, so the GitHub fast tier used by merges never executes it; a regression in tools/rig_check.sh is only caught when the full nightly suite runs. The sprint scope forbids Makefile changes, so this is a follow-up, not a defect of this sprint.
findings.evidence: Makefile:55 'ci-fast:' lists no rig-check-control; mk/m45.mk:54-57 defines the target and hangs it off 'test'; the sprint executor measured 'ci-fast membership of rig-check-control: 0' (sprint JSON MS3 notes).

findings.summary: Sprint artifacts are not in a 'completed' shape: sprint status is 'approved', MS3 is 'measured; landing pending evaluation', and no milestone carries passes/completed fields. The plan defers landing (CHANGELOG, doc move to design_docs/implemented/r1/, README index row) until after this cross-family evaluation, so this is expected, but the JSON cannot show completion at evaluation time.
findings.evidence: JSON key inspection: top-level keys include velocity, critical_path, progress, evaluation_round_1; milestones carry id/title/status/acceptance_criteria/verify/notes but no passes/completed; MS3 status is 'measured; landing pending evaluation' and MS3 notes say the landing is NOT done.

mutants.mutation: M5 (from the design doc): sed 's/-$pid/$pid/g' on a copy of tools/rig_check.sh - the group kill is dropped, so only the direct child (make) is signalled
mutants.evidence: copy differs from the original (cmp rc 1); control rc 1, 'rig-check control: 18 cases, 6 failures'; each hang case reports 'hang child <pid> still alive', i.e. the recipe's child survives because only make was killed

mutants.mutation: M8 (judge's own design, not among the doc's M1-M7): the whole bounded() helper is replaced by a plain 'perl -e "alarm shift; exec @ARGV"' - no process group, no TERM->KILL escalation, the failure mode the doc's own comment calls out ('a plain alarm+exec signals make, not its recipes')
mutants.evidence: copy differs from the original (cmp rc 1); control rc 1, 'rig-check control: 18 cases, 6 failures' with the same five hang cases reporting 'hang child <pid> still alive' (base pass alone: 17 cases, 5 failures).
